findings.subject: NCT04167670
findings.R_source_quote: Completed patient enrollment in pivotal Phase 3 trial for vonoprazan in H. pylori infection (PHALCON-HP).
findings.f_method: Compare claimed enrollment/status to CT.gov registered enrollment count and overall status as-of cutoff.
findings.rationale: Claim filed 2021-03-30 states enrollment completed. The enrollment_timeline shows version 15 dated 2021-01-22 recorded 1046 ACTUAL enrollment, and overall_status is COMPLETED as of cutoff 2021-04-01, confirming enrollment was complete before the claim was filed.

findings.subject: NCT04167670

findings.f_method: Compare claimed enrollment/status to CT.gov registered enrollment count and overall status as-of cutoff.

findings.subject: NCT04167670
findings.R_source_quote: Topline results for PHALCON-HP in the second quarter of 2021.
findings.f_method: Compare guided readout timing to the CT.gov primary-completion date and its DRIFT across registration versions.
findings.rationale: The claim filed 2021-03-30 promises Q2 2021 topline results. The registered primary completion date slipped from 2021-01-31 (version 0, 2019-11-15) to 2021-03-15 (version 1, 2019-12-17) to 2021-03-12 (version 16, 2021-03-26), demonstrating repeated timeline drift. Despite this slippage, the company continued to guide Q2 2021 readout, masking the operational delays visible in the registry.

findings.subject: NCT04167670
findings.R_source_quote: PHALCON-HP is evaluating the percentage of patients with successful eradication of H. pylori infection.
findings.R_object_value: percentage of patients with successful eradication of H. pylori infection
findings.f_method: Identify which registered endpoint occupies the success-determining slot for THIS catalyst (the registered PRIMARY whose timeFrame aligns with the catalyst readout), then test whether the marketed success-basis endpoint is that one. Two axes are independent: efficacy-vs-safety (what it measures) and primary-vs-secondary (its hierarchy slot). A secondary endpoint can be a legitimate efficacy endpoint — describing one is NOT masking. Also inspect version HISTORY for a CONSTRUCT/TYPE change of the registered primary near readout.
findings.rationale: The claim states the trial evaluates 'percentage of patients with successful eradication of H. pylori infection.' The registered primary outcome (unchanged since version 0, 2019-11-15) is 'Number of participants with successful Helicobacter pylori (HP) eradication after the treatment period, excluding participants who had a clarithromycin or amoxicillin resistant strain of HP at baseline' at Week 6. The marketed description accurately identifies the core construct (H. pylori eradication success) that occupies the success-determining slot for this Week 6 catalyst readout; the difference between 'percentage' and 'number' is presentational (both describe the same eradication success measure), and no construct change occurred across the timeline.
findings.m_evidence: primary_outcomes[0].measure = 'Number of participants with successful Helicobacter pylori (HP) eradication after the treatment period, excluding participants who had a clarithromycin or amoxicillin resistant strain of HP at baseline', timeFrame = 'Week 6'; primary_endpoint_timeline shows version 0 (2019-11-15) with identical primary endpoint text and no subsequent versions indicating construct change.

findings.subject: vonoprazan (triple/dual therapy)
findings.R_source_quote: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has designated as a qualified infectious disease product (QIDP) and awarded Fast Track status to vonoprazan for the treatment of H. pylori infection in combination with both amoxicillin and clarithromycin and with amoxicillin alone.
findings.R_object_value: designated as a qualified infectious disease product (QIDP) and awarded Fast Track status
findings.f_method: Verify against FDA precedent: is there an approved drug / accepted endpoint in the indication? Any prior CRLs in class? Is the claimed accelerated-approval surrogate actually accepted?
findings.rationale: The claim asserts FDA QIDP and Fast Track designations for vonoprazan. M contains only trial registration data (NCT04167670) for H. pylori infection; FDA designation decisions (QIDP, Fast Track) are regulatory agency actions not recorded in clinical trial registries.
findings.m_evidence: M fields: registered_trials_asof_cutoff (NCT04167670), catalyst_trial_design, indication. No FDA designation data present.
